capabilities: Wrap tag-shaped text in code spans or code blocks on paste
Repair notes already broken by raw HTML via a command
Handle pastes from rendered HTML sources where the tag survives Obsidian's HTML conversion
Configure detection scope, an ignore list, and confirmation prompts
Toggle protection from the status bar or a command
disambiguation: Not a security or HTML-sanitizing tool; it only rewrites tag-shaped text into code so the renderer ignores it.
extras: The manifest notes the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff, and the README states it was built with AI assistance (Claude, DeepSeek, Poolside).
motivation: The author hit the angle-bracket rendering problem in day-to-day use and built the plugin to fix it.
problem: Pasted text containing something like <name> is parsed as an unclosed raw-HTML tag, so everything below it in the note stops rendering correctly.

relations.evidence: Build setup, release workflow, and manifest.json / versions.json conventions follow the Obsidian sample plugin (MIT).

summary: Paste handler that wraps tag-shaped HTML text in code spans or code blocks so raw angle brackets don't break a note's rendering.
